Moustiquaires imprégnées d’insecticide : 99,9 % de taux de distribution enregistrés dans le Mô
items.description: Djarkpanga, 26 juil. (ATOP) – Le taux de distribution de Moustiquaires imprégnées d’insecticide (MII) dans la préfecture de Mô s’élève à 99,9 %, a affirmé le Comité local d’organisation (CLO) de la campagne dédiée, lors de sa réunion consacrée au bilan de ses activités, le jeudi 22 juillet à Djarkpanga. Les membres du CLO en pleine réunion Dirigée par le secrétaire général de la préfecture Salifou Charifou, représentant le préfet de Mô, la réunion a regroupé les chefs services, les chefs cantons et les responsables des forces de défense et de sécurité. Elle a permis de faire la situation de la campagne de distribution de MII dans le district sanitaire préfectoral, de relever les difficultés rencontrées et de formuler des recommandations. Il est ressorti des présentations que 13.271 ménages sur 13.290 recensés ont reçu 35.254 moustiquaires, soit un taux élogieux de distribution de 99,9 %. Malgré quelques difficultés logistiques et la pluie au cours de la campagne, les résultats obtenus sont satisfaisants, d’après le CLO. Le comité a recommandé la poursuite de la distribution de MII au reste des ménages et de la sensibilisation pour l’utilisation effective des moustiquaires reçues. ATOP/MEK/GMM/DHK

items.title: CAN féminine 2026 : les Lionnes chutent d’entrée contre l’Algérie
items.description: L'équipe nationale féminine du Sénégal a manqué son entrée en lice à la Coupe d'Afrique des nations (CAN) féminine 2026 en s'inclinant face à l'Algérie, ce dimanche, lors de la première journée du groupe A disputée au Maroc. Ce revers complique la situation des Lionnes, qui devront impérativement se relancer lors de leur prochaine sortie face au Kenya, prévue le 30 juillet. Opposées à une sélection algérienne déterminée, les joueuses sénégalaises n'ont pas réussi à prendre les trois points pour lancer idéalement leur campagne continentale. Cette défaite place désormais les Lionnes dans l'obligation de réagir afin de préserver leurs chances de qualification pour les quarts de finale. Avant le coup d'envoi de cette CAN, le Sénégal avait pourtant affiché de solides ambitions malgré une préparation compliquée, marquée par deux défaites en matches amicaux face au Nigeria, champion d'Afrique en titre. Le staff technique espérait voir son équipe monter en puissance au fil de la compétition, mais cette première sortie laisse déjà peu de marge d'erreur. Le prochain rendez-vous s'annonce décisif. Le 30 juillet, les Lionnes affronteront le Kenya, également membre du groupe A. Une victoire sera essentielle pour relancer la campagne sénégalaise avant le dernier match de poule contre le pays hôte, le Maroc, annoncé comme l'un des favoris du tournoi. Le Sénégal dispute sa cinquième phase finale de CAN féminine, la troisième consécutive, preuve des progrès réalisés ces dernières années par le football féminin national. Les Lionnes ambitionnent de franchir un nouveau cap dans cette compétition, qui sert également de qualification pour la Coupe du monde féminine 2027. Pour espérer poursuivre l'aventure, les Sénégalaises devront rapidement corriger les insuffisances affichées lors de cette première journée et retrouver davantage d'efficacité face au but. Le duel contre le Kenya s'annonce déjà comme un véritable tournant dans leur parcours à la CAN 2026.

items.title: Nationwide deaths this monsoon cross 100; more rain likely in country's upper parts from July 29
items.description: As monsoon showers continued to hit parts of the country, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) on Sunday reported seven more casualties in Punjab and three in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, taking the countrywide death toll since June 26 to above 100. According to an NDMA daily situation report covering 24 hours up till 1pm, Punjab’s Gujrat and Okara districts recorded two deaths each, while one casualty each was reported from Sargodha, Narowal and Sialkot. In KP, Hangu registered two deaths and Shangla one. The NDMA specified that the causes behind the casualties were house collapses, electrocutions and drowning. Moreover, at least 47 people were injured in various districts across Punjab, while three individuals were hurt in KP’s Hangu in the 24-hour period. The country has recorded 107 deaths in total during the monsoon rains since June 26, the NDMA data showed. KP recorded the highest number of casualties with 55 deaths, followed by 36 in Punjab, seven in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), six in Balochistan, two in Sindh and one in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB). Over half of the deaths were caused by house/roof collapses, NDMA said. Cumulative deaths and injuries reported across the country between June 26 and July 26, 2026. — Screengrab from NDMA report Meanwhile, the Emergency Response Committee (ERC) constituted earlier this month to oversee coordinated response during monsoon held its fifth meeting today at the NDMA headquarters, a press release from the Prime Minister’s Office said. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal chaired the meeting via video link. Climate Change Minister Dr Musadik Malik, National Food Security Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain, and IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja also joined the meeting via video link. NDMA Chairman Lt General Inam Haider Malik, along with senior officials of the authority, representatives of relevant federal and provincial departments, and other key stakeholders, attended the meeting. The ERC reviewed the implementation status of preparedness measures undertaken by Provincial Disaster Management Authorities (PDMAs) and other relevant departments, the PMO said. Provincial representatives presented updates on the availability of relief supplies, emergency communication mechanisms, evacuation planning, response readiness, and inter-agency coordination to ensure timely and effective response during the ongoing monsoon season. Fresh wet spell likely to commence from July 29 Separately, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) forecast that a fresh wet spell was likely to commence from July 29 in the upper catchments of all major rivers, as well as Islamabad, upper Punjab, AJK, KP and GB. However, “no flood-generating” rainfall activity was expected till July 28 (Tuesday). Meanwhile, for up to Monday noon, the PMD predicted “scattered” rain-wind/thunderstorms over the upper catchment of all major rivers, along with Islamabad, AJK and GB. Here is the province-wise forecast by the Met Office for the 24 hours till around Monday noon: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Abbottabad, Batagram, Buner, Chitral, Haripur, Kohat, Kohistan, Mansehra, Mardan, Nowshera, Shangla, Swabi, Swat, Tor Ghar and Dir. Punjab Attock, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Chakwal, Chiniot, Dera Ghazi Khan, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad, Jhang, Jhelum, Kasur, Khanewal, Khushab, Lahore, Lodhran, Mandi Bahauddin, Multan, Muzaffargarh, Nankana Sahib, Narowal, Okara, Pakpattan, Rawalpindi, Sahiwal, Sargodha, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Toba Tek Singh and Vehari. Sindh Badin, Hyderabad, Matiari, Mirpurkhas, Sanghar, Tando Allahyar, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tharparkar and Umerkot. For Karachi, the Met Office, in a separate advisory, forecast cloudy and humid weather with light rain/drizzle and chances of thunderstorms/rain at the outskirts of the city on Sunday. On Monday and Tuesday, the weather in the metropolis will continue to remain cloudy with chances of isolated drizzle. Balochistan Barkhan, Duki, Kalat, Khuzdar, Kohlu, Loralai and Musakhel. Major rivers at normal to low flood levels As of 6pm, PMD’s Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) said most major rivers were flowing at either normal or low flood level. However, River Ravi recorded a medium-level flood with increasing water flows at Sidhnai headworks. The levels at Jassar and Shahdara were normal, while Balloki was in low flood. River Indus was recorded at normal at three barrages and in low flood at four other points. Jhelum and Sutlej were at normal levels. Water flows in River Chenab had also subsided, reaching a low-level flood at Marala, Khanki, Qadirabad, and Trimmu barrages. In its update at 11:30am, the PMD had said that River Indus at Kalabagh, Chashma, Taunsa and Guddu were expected to remain in low flood levels for the next 48 hours. However, the Met Office placed rivers Chenab and Ravi on a high-risk level on its flood severity scale. In a statement on Sunday morning, Punjab’s Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) said that while the rivers in the province continued to flood due to rain, the flow in the waterways had remained stable in the previous 24 hours. PDMA added that there was a medium flood situation in Narowal’s Basantar Nullah while a high-level flood persisted in Wazirabad’s Phalko Nullah, with a flow of 5,000 cusecs. The PDMA statement also carried its director general’s appeal to citizens residing in the floodplains to immediately evacuate to safer places, adding that the provincial government had made all necessary arrangements for affected areas. “All basic facilities and medicines will be provided in the flood relief camps,” the PDMA DG was quoted as saying. In a separate statement, the authority said that 115mm of rain was recorded in Noorpur Thal, 107mm in Gujranwala, 94mm in Gujrat, 68mm in Narowal, 65mm in Mandi Bahauddin, 52mm in Sialkot Airport, 46mm in Okara, 40mm in Jauharabad and 38mm in Sargodha during the last 24 hours. Meanwhile, Lahore received 37mm of rainfall, Mangla 37mm, Jhelum 32mm, Sheikhupura 28mm, Hafizabad and Kasur 27mm, Chakwal 20mm, Bahawalnagar 18mm and Khanewal 16mm, the spokesperson said. “A total of 450 mm of rain was recorded in Lahore over a period of 5 days,” the statement said, adding that Rawalpindi, Faisalabad, Multan, Attock, Murree and Bahawalpur also received rainfall. PDMA also cautioned of the risk of flooding in rivers and canals in low-lying areas due to rain, as well as landslides in mountainous areas such as Murree. Heavy rain may also damage mud-brick houses, it added.

items.title: Niger/An 3 du CNSP: le Président Tiani réaffirme l’implication de la France dans les tentatives de déstabilisation du Sahel
items.description: NIGER-AN3-CNSP-ENTRETIEN-PRESIDENT-TIANI Niger/An 3 du CNSP: le Président Tiani réaffirme l’implication de la France dans les tentatives de déstabilisation du Sahel Ouagadougou, 26 juil. (AIB) – Le Président de la République du Niger, le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, a réaffirmé, samedi 25 juillet 2026, dans un entretien accordé à la Télévision nationale à l’occasion du 3ᵉ anniversaire du Conseil National pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (CNSP), l’implication de la France et de certains pays occidentaux dans les tentatives de déstabilisation du Sahel. Le Chef de l’État a salué la résilience du peuple nigérien et sahélien ainsi que le sacrifice des Forces de défense, rendant hommage aux soldats tombés pour leurs patries. Cette lutte, a-t-il affirmé, « donne des résultats malgré l’adversité féroce et acharnée de certains pays occidentaux et particulièrement européens ». Le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, a réaffirmé l'implication la France et d’autres pays occidentaux dans le « sponsoring du terrorisme qui endeuille le Sahel », rappelant des faits ou des propos tenus par plusieurs dirigeants européens avec à leur tête le président Emmanuel Macron, exprimant leur volonté de perturber la stabilité au Sahel Parmi les tentatives de déstabilisation, il a cité le délai d’une semaine donné par la France au Niger, après le renversement de l’ancien régime, pour « rétablir Bazoum, au cas contraire, la foudre allait s’abattre sur nous ». La France s’était également servie de la CEDEAO pour exiger le rétablissement de l’ordre constitutionnel au Niger, a-t-il indiqué. Selon le Président du Niger, ce combat pour la dignité, l'indépendance, et la souveraineté « n’est pas que le combat d'Assimi Goïta, d’Ibrahim Traoré ou de Tiani », mais celui de toute l’Afrique. Évoquant l’attaque du 18 juin 2026 contre l’aéroport international Diori Hamani de Niamey, il a souligné que les assaillants étaient des « marionnettes » regroupées, entraînées et financées par la France, selon des éléments de preuve détenus par les autorités nigériennes. La France, a-t-il poursuivi, « va utiliser tous les moyens, comme Emmanuel Macron l’a dit, et je le cite : qu’il ne quittera pas le pouvoir avant de régler les comptes aux dirigeants du Niger prioritairement, ensuite ceux du Sahel, c’est-à-dire Assimi Goïta et Ibrahim Traoré ». Il a expliqué que l’attaque devait viser simultanément l’aéroport, le palais de la Présidence et le centre d’instruction et de formation des officiers de Tondibia. Les assaillants ont reçu des moyens de communication fournis par les renseignements français, a précisé le Chef de l'État nigérien. Selon lui, une partie du commando a été interpellée deux jours avant l’attaque, tandis qu’un autre groupe a été repéré près de l’aéroport. Le Chef de l’État a affirmé que l’attaque visait notamment à montrer que la sécurité du Niger était conditionnée à la présence des militaires occidentaux, après leur expulsion de la base aérienne de Niamey. Elle devait également alimenter la guerre informationnelle visant à montrer l’incapacité des Africains à s’auto-déterminer et à détruire l’aéroport, point stratégique reliant le Niger au reste du monde. Le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani, a estimé que cette attaque pourrait ne pas être la dernière, car « l’objectif visé par la France n’est toujours pas atteint et elle fera toujours face à notre détermination ». Agence d'information du Burkina BAK/ata Source: ANP

items.title: Modi announces panel to reform India's exam system; anti-govt graffiti at Jantar Mantar painted over
items.description: India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday a special task force to reform the country’s exam system, a day after his government’s education minister resigned . The social media-driven Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had drawn thousands of demonstrators, mainly students, to the capital’s Jantar Mantar site in New Delhi, forming one of India’s largest anti-government protests in recent years. Modi said in a video posted to X that his administration “decided to set up a high-powered task force” led by Nandan Nilekani — the co-founder of India’s IT giant Infosys — “which will focus on examination reform”. “Our examination system must be reliable. Our examination system must be transparent. Our examination system must make maximum use of technology,” Modi added in the video statement. Modi said the government “will work to ensure the credibility of upcoming examinations as quickly as possible”. Weeks of protests over exam irregularities and other issues affecting young Indians culminated on Saturday with the resignation of the education minister and the government accepting other key demands. The movement sparked by a call for education reforms evolved to include concerns over unemployment, opportunities for young people and what critics brand as Modi’s increasingly authoritarian style of governance. Protest site cleared On Sunday, dozens of municipal workers were washing the pavements along the road leading to the site, where activists had camped for weeks and where just hours earlier the crowd sang protest songs, chanted slogans and painted acerbic graffiti. “We have been here since midnight when the protesters left,” a municipal worker who declined to be identified told AFP . “The walls have been painted, but may require another coat of paint as some lines [from the slogans] are still visible,” he said. Nayan Thakrele, 19, one of many young people who had come from across India to join the movement, finally reached Jantar Mantar on Sunday morning. “It’s a shame that the protest is over by the time I reached here,” Thakrele, who took a 20-hour train journey from the central state of Madhya Pradesh, told AFP . “I first heard about it on Instagram and saw the electrifying atmosphere, colourful walls, posters, and wanted to be here and experience it myself,” Thakrele said. ‘Face the electoral consequences’ Amish, 35, had also hoped to join the protests but reached the site when it was already being painted clean. “I had booked the flight from Mumbai before Pradhan’s resignation,” he told AFP . Amish said that the Modi government had backed itself into a corner with its response to the protests, which at times escalated into brief clashes and outbursts of violence. “Had they not tried a crackdown, the protest wouldn’t have become as big as it did,” said Amish. “I feel that this government will now face the electoral consequences of its recent actions.” A Delhi police constable at Jantar Mantar said that only a few people came there on Sunday morning, “mostly locals who are curious to see the site they’d seen in protest videos online”. Now painted red, the wall behind the constable was used by demonstrators to put up posters and notes, including of police officers who had baton-charged or used tear gas against protesters. “We want everything to be documented and remembered,” protester Rahul told AFP on Saturday near the so-called “wall of shame”. “We have taken photos and videos of these posters and hope everyone shares them widely.”

(ATOP) – Le conseil municipal de la commune Agoè-Nyivé 6 a entamé, le samedi 25 juillet, une tournée de sensibilisation des contribuables sur la « Participation citoyenne au développement de la commune ». la participation citoyenne au développement local des contribuables pour la mobilisation des fonds destines à. La tournée qui prendra fin le 16 août prochain, va permettre de présenter aux administrés, les onze membres du conseil municipal. Le but est de les sensibiliser sur le projet de mobilisation de fonds destiné à l’acquisition d’une machine dénommée « Grader » pour l’entretien des routes de la commune. Remise Symbolique Cette tournée a démarré à Tonoukouti, et se poursuit dans les villages de Kpotavé, Lomégnokopé, Adzovè, Kladjémé, Agotimé, Agnavé, Tsikplonou Kondji, Dévimé, Kpokpomé, Adoglové et Adékopé Centre. Le maire de la commune Agoè-Nyivé 6, Songoï Kézié a salué la mobilisation des populations et les a remerciées pour la confiance qu’elles accordent au conseil municipal. Il a indiqué que cette tournée traduit la volonté de l’exécutif communal de rapprocher davantage les administrateurs des administrés. « Le développement de notre commune ne peut être l’affaire des seuls élus. Il est l’engagement et la participation de tous », a-t-il indiqué. Le conseiller municipal, Gnon Adoh Samuel a exprimé sa gratitude à la population pour la confiance placée en eux. Selon lui, le coût du Grader est estimé à 100 millions de FCFA, dont 50% reviennent à la mairie et les 50 % restants aux contribuables et partenaires. Il a invité chaque citoyen à soutenir ce projet qui permettra d’améliorer ou d’entretenir des routes et de favoriser le développement socio-économique de la commune. Le chef du canton d’Adéticopé, Togbuigan Assimadji et celui du village de Tonoukouti, Togbui Takpoe François IV ont salué cette initiative de proximité qui renforce le dialogue entre les élus locaux et les contribuables. Ils ont exhorté les populations à accompagner la mairie dans la réalisation de ce projet. Les échanges ont permis aux habitants de soumettre plusieurs doléances relatives, entre autres, à l’installation de poteaux électriques, au renforcement de la sécurité, à la construction de marchés ainsi qu’à la création de collèges et lycées. La tournée se déroule chaque week-end dans les différents villages de la commune. ATOP/ASA/GMM/DHK

items.title: Los incendios de Madrid, Ávila y Toledo obligan a evacuar o confinar a 90.000 personas
items.description: Los grandes incendios forestales que arrasan la provincia de Ávila y la Comunidad de Madrid siguen activos . Sí se han logrado contener muchos de los frentes, aunque se mantienen activas “varias cabezas” y no pueden darse por perimetrados. Desde hace cuatro días, las fuertes rachas de viento dificultan la extinción y los bomberos encadenan jornadas de trabajo extenuantes . Los esfuerzos del operativo están este domingo centrados de nuevo en proteger poblaciones, evacuar de forma preventiva y evitar que las llamas de ambos se fusionen. Aun así, la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) los trata y coordina como un único fuego, y el Gobierno ha ampliado la emergencia nacional a Toledo. Entre las tres regiones, hay afectadas ya 77.000 hectáreas y alrededor de 90.000 evacuados o confinados, según los últimos datos de Interior , que rebajan ligeramente la cifra estimada el sábado por la noche por las autoridades madrileñas. Solo en Ávila, son 50.000 hectáreas, lo que lo convierte en el mayor incendio de la historia de España. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Troops arrest two suspected terrorist informants, cattle rustlers, in Yobe market
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Damaturu Troops of Operation HADIN KAI have arrested two suspected terrorist informants and cattle rustlers during a joint operation with local hunters at the Buni Yadi Friday Market in Gujba Local Government Area of Yobe State. Military sources on Sunday revealed that the operation was carried out at about 2:00 p.m. on July 24 by troops of 27 Task Force Brigade in conjunction with members of a hunters’ group acting on intelligence. The suspects were identified as Muhammadu Sani, 32, from Mainahari village in Biu Local Government Area of Borno State, and Buba Umaru, 40, from Garin Jauro in Fune Local Government Area of Yobe State. According to the sources, the operation turned violent when one of the suspects attacked a member of the hunters’ group with a cutlass while resisting arrest. The hunter sustained severe head injuries during the attack and was immediately attended to, while the troops overpowered and apprehended the suspects. Preliminary investigations revealed that Muhammadu Sani confessed to serving as a logistics supplier and informant for Boko Haram terrorists for nearly seven years. He also admitted to leading terrorists to the residences of two local residents, where the insurgents successfully rustled cattle during separate attacks. Military sources said the confession is expected to assist ongoing intelligence efforts aimed at dismantling terrorist support networks operating within communities across the North-East. The two suspects are currently in the custody of 27 Task Force Brigade and are undergoing further investigation to determine the extent of their involvement in terrorist logistics, intelligence gathering, and cattle rustling activities. Security officials said the arrest underscores the critical role played by local intelligence and collaboration between troops and community-based security groups in identifying individuals who provide logistical support and operational information to terrorist elements. items.title: Championnats du monde de Scrabble : le Sénégal décroche quatre médailles d’or et une d’argent à Tunis
items.description: Le Sénégal confirme son statut de place forte du Scrabble francophone. Aux Championnats du monde disputés à Tunis, la délégation sénégalaise a réalisé une nouvelle moisson de médailles, marquée par le sacre d'Abdou Faye et de Boubacar Mané dans l'épreuve des Paires de la catégorie Diamant. Ce nouveau titre vient couronner une compétition exceptionnelle pour Abdou Faye. Déjà sacré champion du monde en Blitz puis en Élite dans la catégorie Diamant, le champion sénégalais ajoute une troisième médaille d'or à son palmarès en s'imposant aux côtés de Boubacar Mané. Une performance qui confirme sa domination sur la scène mondiale du Scrabble. Au-delà de ses exploits sportifs, Abdou Faye affiche également un parcours professionnel remarquable. Ancien cadre de l'Administration des Impôts et Domaines, énarque et ex-professeur de fiscalité, il a notamment eu parmi ses étudiants l'actuel président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Une anecdote qu'il raconte avec le sourire, confiant qu'il souhaiterait un jour retrouver son ancien élève autour d'un plateau de Scrabble. Grâce à cette nouvelle médaille d'or, la délégation sénégalaise boucle son séjour à Tunis avec un bilan impressionnant de cinq médailles, dont quatre en or et une en argent. La médaille d'argent est revenue à Mamadou Mbengue, participant à cette campagne historique qui témoigne de la régularité du Sénégal au plus haut niveau. Les autres représentants sénégalais n'ont pas été en reste. Les frères Sylla ont décroché une honorable cinquième place en catégorie Élite, illustrant la richesse du vivier national. De son côté, Ndongo a signé un retour remarqué en compétition internationale. Après plusieurs années d'absence, il a livré des prestations saluées par les observateurs, démontrant que son expérience et son talent restent intacts. Avec ces nouveaux résultats, le Sénégal consolide un peu plus sa réputation de référence mondiale du Scrabble francophone. Les performances enregistrées à Tunis illustrent non seulement l'excellence de ses champions, mais aussi la solidité d'une école sénégalaise qui continue de dominer les grandes compétitions internationales.

items.title: 42-year-old man jailed 10 years for defiling 7-year-old boy in Wa
items.description: The Wa High Court has sentenced a 42-year-old man, Elyasu Kunateh, to 10 years’ imprisonment in hard labour for the defilement of a seven-year-old boy in Wa in the Upper West Region. According to the Upper West Regional Police Command, through the Regional Domestic Violence and Victims Support Unit (DOVVSU), the convict was found guilty after a full trial before the Wa High Court. The Police said the incident occurred on Saturday, 17th January 2026, and was reported by the victim’s mother, leading to the arrest of Kunateh on Tuesday, 20 January 2026. “Upon receiving the complaint, the Police immediately commenced investigations and referred the victim to a medical facility for examination, in addition to offering him psychosocial support,” the Command stated. The accused was subsequently remanded into police custody after being put before the court. The Presiding Judge, Justice Osei-Wusu Antwi, on Thursday, 23rd July 2026, convicted Kunateh and sentenced him to 10 years in hard labour. The Upper West Regional Police Command has reaffirmed its commitment to protecting vulnerable persons and pursuing cases involving child abuse, sexual offences and gender-based violence. The Command has also urged parents, guardians, caregivers and members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspected cases of abuse to the nearest police station for immediate action.

items.title: Última hora de los incendios forestales, en directo | El incendio de Ávila es ya el mayor de la historia de España con 50.000 hectáreas quemadas
items.description: El incendio declarado en Burgohondo (Ávila) ha quemado ya unas 50.000 hectáreas, una cifra que convierte este fuego en el mayor de la historia de España desde que se tienen registros, según ha confirmado Sara Aagesen, ministra para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (Miteco). Aagesen ha advertido además de que España atraviesa una campaña de fuegos “extraordinariamente complicada”. Según ha explicado, se han calcinado 153.000 hectáreas en lo que va de año, una superficie seis veces superior a la registrada en el mismo periodo de 2025, y se han contabilizado 32 grandes incendios forestales. El delegado del Gobierno en Madrid, Francisco Martín, ha afirmado este domingo que la principal preocupación del operativo de extinción se sitúa en el entorno del pantano de San Juan, donde los equipos trabajan para evitar que las reactivaciones del incendio compliquen la evolución del fuego hacia el norte del embalse. El teniente coronel de la UME Alfonso Arribas ha asegurado que todos los frentes del incendio que afecta a la Comunidad de Madrid y Ávila están contenidos, aunque persisten varias cabezas activas. ADC to Tinubu: You’re becoming a professional statement-maker on insecurity
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused President Bola Tinubu of becoming ‘a professional statement-maker’ on insecurity, demanding timelines and regular updates on efforts to rescue 176 residents of Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State who have remained in captivity since they were abducted on February 3, 2026. For the ADC, the issue is not that some abductees have been rescued. It is that families whose relatives have spent months in captivity say they are still waiting for answers. The party argued that the government cannot celebrate one rescue while leaving other victims wondering whether they have been forgotten, insisting that every Nigerian life deserves the same urgency and attention. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the opposition party linked its concerns to Friday’s peaceful protest by Kaiama residents over the fate of the 176 abductees, saying recent attacks across Kwara, Zamfara, Benue, Kebbi, and Borno states showed that insecurity remained a national emergency rather than isolated incidents. “On one of the defining challenges of this government, the president is increasingly seen as a professional statement-maker, while communities continue to bury their dead, search for the missing, and wait for rescues that never seem to come,” Abdullahi said. The party said President Tinubu’s public celebration of the recent rescue of abductees in Oyo State had inevitably triggered fresh questions about the fate of hundreds of other Nigerians still being held by kidnappers and insurgents across the country. According to the ADC, “Every successful rescue of abducted Nigerians deserves to be celebrated. But the president must ensure that his actions do not create the impression that the value of a Nigerian life depends on where the victim comes from or whether the tragedy attracts national headlines. Leadership demands equal compassion for every citizen.” The party said residents of Kaiama Local Government Area took to the streets on Friday, July 24, in a peaceful protest after more than 170 days without any word on their abducted relatives, describing the demonstration as the desperate cry of families who feared they had been abandoned. “Their protest was not political. It was the cry of citizens who fear that their loved ones have been forgotten,” the statement said. Beyond Kwara, the ADC said the security crisis continued to deepen across the country, pointing to the abduction of at least 40 residents, mostly women and children, from 11 communities in the Mayanchi District of the Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State; renewed attacks in Benue State’s Sankera axis; the kidnapping of Kebbi State High Court Judge Justice Faruku Hassan Bunza from his residence in the early hours of Sunday; and persistent insurgent attacks that have displaced communities in parts of Borno State. Against that backdrop, the party said Nigerians deserved more than reassuring statements from the presidency. “What progress has been made in securing the release of the 176 abductees from Kaiama? What is being done to rescue the women and children taken in Zamfara? What efforts are underway to secure the release of Justice Bunza? What updates are available on victims in Borno and other affected communities?” the ADC asked. “The president owes Nigerians more than broad assurances. He owes them regular updates, timelines, and evidence that no Nigerian community has been abandoned,” it added. The opposition party also questioned President Tinubu’s repeated assurances that insecurity would soon become a thing of the past, arguing that such declarations were steadily losing their reassuring effect because they had not been matched by visible outcomes. “Hope cannot survive indefinitely on declarations alone. There comes a point when repeated assurances, unaccompanied by visible results, cease to reassure. They simply become another headline in a long cycle of official optimism and public disappointment,” the statement added. The ADC urged the President to back his words with decisive action, insisting that those abducted in Kwara, the women and children taken in Zamfara, victims of renewed attacks in Benue, and communities under siege in Borno and Justice Bunza all deserved the same urgency and presidential attention accorded to victims recently rescued elsewhere. “Leadership is not measured by how quickly government celebrates a rescue; it is measured by whether no Nigerian is left behind or forgotten,” the party said. items.title: In reply to Nawaz, Bilawal says people of AJK not ready to 'bargain away their rights' in elections
items.description: MIRPUR: Responding to PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif’s recent jibe , PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday said that whether it’s Kashmir or Kashmore, Mirpur or Mirpurkhas, their residents were “not ready to bargain away their rights”. Bilawal’s response comes a day before the first phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) is set to begin, with Mirpur voting on Monday. It also comes amid allegations of pre-poll rigging by the PPP after the PML-N gave 10 e-buses to Muzaffarabad and Mirpur as a “gift”. Addressing a public rally in AJK’s Mirpur on Friday as part of his party’s election campaign, Nawaz had named Bilawal and said Kashmir should not be mistaken for Kashmore, nor Mirpur for Mirpurkhas — districts of Sindh where the PPP has been in power for years. Subsequently, Bilawal shared a video statement on social media, beginning his message with, “ Mian sahib , please don’t take offence”, as he tagged Nawaz’s X account in his post. “Whether it’s Kashmir or Kashmore, Mirpur or Mirpurkhas, not only do their names resemble each other; their temperament matches too, their honour matches too, and so does the courage to stand up for their rights,” he said. The PPP chairman added: “Whether it’s Kashmore or Kashmir, no one would let anyone rob them politically of their right to governance and right to ownership. “Whether it’s Kashmir or Kashmore, Mirpur or Mirpurkhas, their people are not ready to bargain away their rights. They want to make their own decisions. They will not hand over power over their future to any other city, nor any other province.” The Bhutto scion asserted, “Just as in the previous elections the people of Kashmir and Kashmore rejected the Muslim League, just as the [PML-N] was swept away in Mirpur and Mirpurkhas, the people will repeat that same verdict in the upcoming elections too.” Referring to tomorrow’s polls in Mirpur, Bilawal expressed his belief that the “Kashmir’s verdict would be in favour of the PPP and just like in Mirpurkhas, the people of Mirpur would hunt the lion with the arrow”. In another post before that, Bilawal also directly commented on Nawaz and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s announcement of “gifting” electric buses and hospitals on wheels to people of AJK before the election. Ten e-buses arrived in Muzaffarabad on Saturday, while more reached Mirpur today, the PML-N said. In his post, Bilawal said, “You are being promised buses, hospitals, roads, and an airport. I welcome every bus, every hospital, every road, and every airport. “But something built with the public’s money is not a gift from any politician — it is the public’s right.” “The PPP has not just made promises,” he remarked, emphasising that the party — which is currently in power in the region — had included 3,308 additional teachers, a cardiac hospital, new roads, IT centres, and employment opportunities for the youth in AJK’s budget. “I myself secured funding for Mirpur Airport in the previous federal budget. The very stadium where our opponents hold their rallies was also built during the PPP’s tenure.” The PPP chairman reiterated that he wanted to secure for the people of Kashmir the right to governance, the right to ownership, and the right to employment. “The same rights that every Pakistani citizen is entitled to. Then they won’t need gifts of this sort. They will arrange their own development.” Bilawal urged his supporters to come out in large numbers on polling day to cast their votes for his party. “Progress too! Authority too! Employment too! And Kashmir’s decision by Kashmiris!” Mirpur division gears up for first phase of polls Separately, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on Sunday urged voters in Mirpur division to turn out in large numbers for the first phase of the general elections tomorrow, in which more than 1.4 million registered voters will elect representatives from 13 constituencies. In a video message, the CEC said elaborate security arrangements had been made for the polls, with security forces and Quick Response Force teams deployed at polling stations and security also being ensured for voters travelling to and from polling stations. He warned that anyone attempting to disrupt the polling process would face legal action. According to the AJK Election Commission, 1,400,437 voters — including 724,811 men and 675,626 women — were registered in the division’s 13 constituencies. Polling will be held at 2,316 polling stations, of which 1,241 have been declared highly sensitive, 724 sensitive and 351 normal. A total of 288 candidates are contesting the elections. Election monitoring has been organised through 13 zones and 205 sectors across the division, while 18,560 personnel from police and other law enforcement agencies have been deployed under a three-tier security plan. Under the arrangement, police will provide the first layer of security, Pakistan Rangers (Punjab), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the Federal Constabulary the second, and the Pakistan Army the third. Around 2,100 army personnel will also be deployed, while Quick Response Force teams will remain on standby to respond to any emergency. Chief Secretary Khushal Khan and Election Commission Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel informed the media that all arrangements had been finalised for the first phase of the elections, with polling material delivered to returning officers, election personnel deployed and security put on high alert. Addressing a joint press conference in Muzaffarabad earlier in the day, the chief secretary said electioneering had reached its peak across the region, with corner meetings, banners, posters and party flags visible in various areas, while the leadership of major federal political parties had also visited AJK to campaign. He warned that authorities were closely monitoring misleading propaganda about the elections on social media and said strict legal action would be taken against anyone attempting to disrupt the polling process or disturb public order. He maintained that all state institutions were fully prepared to ensure transparent, free and peaceful elections. Shakeel said around 22,000 election personnel had been deployed and polling material had already reached polling stations. He added that CEC Mughal had recently visited Mirpur to review the arrangements and expressed satisfaction over the preparations. He clarified that an old video calling for an election boycott was being circulated on social media to create a false impression, insisting that election campaigns had continued peacefully across all districts without any untoward incident. Shakeel said all political parties and candidates had welcomed the Election Commission’s code of conduct, while members of the public themselves were lodging complaints against elements attempting to obstruct the electoral process, reflecting public confidence in the election system. Meanwhile, the Election Commission allowed registered political parties, candidates and election agents to use automated telephone calls, commonly known as robocalls, for election campaigning until 48 hours before polling day. In a statement, the commission said the decision was taken after considering an application submitted by PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin and PPP Secretary General Nayyer Hussain Bukhari under Clause 17 of the Election Code of Conduct 2026. The commission said the permission allows campaign messages to be delivered through pre-recorded voice calls sent automatically to large numbers of voters until the commencement of the mandatory 48-hour campaign silence before polling.

items.title: Osun election: Hoodlums attack PVC collection centre, cart away cards
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Suspected political thugs on Sunday attacked a Permanent Voter’s Card distribution centre in Okuku, Odo-Otin local government area of the state, allegedly carting away two packs of PVCs. It was gathered that the centre, Oyinlola DC Primary School, Ward 2, where INEC was distributing the cards, was invaded by thugs shooting sporadically into the air, scaring residents and officials away. The hoodlums, it was gathered, disrupted the process, took two packs of cards and left the venue before police could arrive at the scene. Confirming the incident, Osun Police Public Relations Officer DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, the command said the incident occurred at Oyinlola DC Primary School, Ward 2, where INEC officials were peacefully distributing permanent voter cards. According to the Command, about ten armed hoodlums invaded the centre, fired sporadically into the air and carted away three packs of PVCs before fleeing the scene. Ojelabi said the commissioner of police, Ibrahim Gotan, has condemned the attack and directed a comprehensive investigation to identify and prosecute those responsible. The Osun State House of Assembly Speaker, Hon. Adewale Egbedun, through his Chief Press Secretary, Olamide Tiamiyu, in a statement, fingered the opposition party, All Progressives Congress (APC), for perpetrating the invasion. He described the incident as a grave assault on Nigeria’s democracy and the sanctity of the electoral process, warning that any attempt to intimidate voters, compromise electoral materials or manipulate the democratic process poses a serious threat to free and fair elections and must not be tolerated. He called on the relevant security agencies to launch an immediate, thorough and impartial investigation into the incident, identify those responsible and ensure they are brought to justice in accordance with the law. Meanwhile, APC, through the head media of its campaign council, Oluremi Omowaiye, speaking with THE NATION, alleged Egbedun for bankrolling hoodlums to disrupt the distribution exercise on Sunday morning. He said, “It is obvious that the Accord Party is losing it every day; hence, its party leader in Odo-Otin, the Speaker, Egbedun, who is known for assaulting people, including his king, recruited thugs to the collection points for disruption. “We urge security agencies to arrest Egbedun and other suspected wanted criminals who are hibernating in the Government House and sharing immunity with Governor Ademola Adeleke.” Also, the INEC REC in the state, Mrs Oluwatoyin Babalola, confirmed and condemned the attack, saying, “As I speak to you, I am waiting for the report of the attack. I cannot say the number of PVCs that were taken away. We want to ascertain the numbers.” Babalola assures that “we are promising people of our two states that we are going to conduct an election that is free, fair, credible, inclusive and transparent.” The post Osun election: Hoodlums attack PVC collection centre, cart away cards appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Suspect in Berlin attack near Pride gathering shot dead by police
items.description: A known suspect in the driving of a minivan into a crowd near a major LGBTQ Pride gathering in Berlin was shot dead by law enforcement officers in the city’s Spandau district, police said on Sunday. The ramming attack happened in the Tiergarten park near the Brandenburg Gate at about 10pm (2000 GMT) on Saturday, not far from one of Europe’s biggest annual LGBTQ celebrations, Christopher Street Day. One person was killed, and 29 were injured, authorities said. “Around 6pm (1600 GMT), the suspect involved in yesterday’s attack in Tiergarten was located at an allotment garden complex in Spandau,” Berlin police wrote on X. “According to initial findings, he ran towards officers while armed with a bladed weapon; police… subsequently opened fire. Despite immediate resuscitation efforts by the Berlin Fire Department, he died at the scene.” A federal prosecutor’s spokesperson confirmed one person had been shot and declared dead. Berlin police had identified the suspect as Abdul B, 21, and published his picture, asking the public for information on his whereabouts. The suspect had “attracted attention in the past through a high number of criminal offences, through radicalisation, through membership of the Islamist scene”, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said earlier, adding that he was a German citizen of Lebanese heritage, born in Germany in 2005. It was the latest in a series of vehicle attacks on crowds in Germany in recent years that have intensified debate around security and immigration amid a surge in support for the far-right . Ahead of a memorial service at St Mary’s Church in Berlin, centre-right Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Germans to protect liberal values. “We will defend the freedom, openness, and liberal spirit of our lives and our society with everything we can do,” he said.

items.title: Les États-Unis se préparent à installer des bases militaires au Maroc
items.description: Les États-Unis se préparent-ils à ouvrir des bases militaires au Maroc ? C’est ce que, en tout cas, déduit la presse marocaine à partir de la teneur du projet de budget américain pour 2027. Selon des médias marocains, le Sénat américain a demandé au Pentagone d’étudier “la création de nouveaux sites de sécurité au Maroc ” qui serviraient à “renforcer la préparation conjointe et la capacité de réaction aux crises régionales”. Washington envisagent de créer des “sites de sécurité” au Maroc Selon la même source, la mesure figure dans la version sénatoriale du budget américain de la défense pour 2027. Dans le texte, il n’est pas fait état explicitement de l’ouverture de bases militaires américaines, mais ses rédacteurs ont imposé l’élaboration d’options pour établir des “sites de sécurité coopérative” au Maroc, selon la lecture faite par le journal en ligne marocain Bladi. Maroc : l’emplacement des sites américains n’a pas été précisé Les sénateurs américains ont également demandé au Pentagone d’étudier la possibilité de “partager les coûts de rénovation de pistes autrefois utilisées au Maroc par le Strategic Air Command américain”. Ni la localisation ni l’ampleur de ces travaux n’ont été précisées. Les États-Unis souhaiteraient également étudier la création d’un vaste complexe d’entraînement multi-domaines, poursuivre la modernisation des forces armées royales par l’acquisition d’équipements militaires américains et la mise en place d’un “centre d’excellence consacré aux drones”, selon la presse marocaine. Le secrétaire américain à la Défense devrait présenter devant le Congrès, dans les 180 jours suivant la promulgation du projet de loi, un plan destiné à approfondir la coopération militaire entre Washington et Rabat, selon Bladi . Cette feuille de route doit s’inscrire dans le partenariat de défense Maroc–États-Unis prévu pour la période 2026-2036. L’article Les États-Unis se préparent à installer des bases militaires au Maroc est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Choc à Karangasso-Sambla : Une tombe profanée pour « libérer la pluie » parce la défunte n’ayant pas de seins
items.description: Le repos éternel a été brutalement interrompu dans la commune de Karangasso-Sambla, située dans la province du Houet. Selon des informations révélées par le journal L'Express du Faso, une sépulture a été la cible d'une profanation le 7 juillet dernier. Des villageois ont exhumé le corps d’une femme au motif que sa morphologie, l’absence de poitrine de son vivant, serait la cause mystique de l'arrêt des pluies dans la localité. Cet acte, accompli au mépris des protestations des descendants, a plongé le village dans une crise sociale latente. L’ambiance est devenue irrespirable à Karangasso-Sambla. Dans cette localité de la province du Houet, le sacré s'est heurté à l'irrationnel le 7 juillet dernier. Une affaire de profanation de tombe, rapportée initialement par le quotidien L’Express du Faso, soulève une vague d’indignation et met en lumière la persistance de croyances radicales au sein de la communauté. Tout commence par un constat climatique : l’arrêt des précipitations. Pour certains habitants, l'explication n'est pas météorologique mais mystique. Ils ont pointé du doigt l'enterrement récent d'une femme sur un site jugé inapproprié. Le grief ? La défunte, de son vivant, « n’avait pas poussé des seins ». Pour les profanateurs, cette caractéristique physique ferait obstacle à la pluie. Malgré l'opposition farouche des descendants de la défunte, les auteurs de l'acte ont procédé à l'exhumation forcée du corps. Au-delà de la profanation, c’est le sort de la dépouille qui suscite aujourd'hui les plus vives inquiétudes. Comme le précise L'Express du Faso, le lieu où le corps a été transporté et ré-enterré demeure inconnu pour une partie de la population et de la famille, ajoutant ainsi le mystère à l'outrage. L’acte n'est pas resté sans conséquences sociales. La commune est actuellement traversée par une crise latente entre deux camps opposés de la population. Entre les défenseurs d'un ordre traditionnel sacrifiant la dignité humaine et ceux réclamant justice pour la mémoire de la défunte, la tension est palpable. Cette affaire, qui mêle superstition et violation flagrante du droit au respect des morts, place désormais les autorités face au défi de ramener la paix sociale dans un climat chargé de ressentiments. items.title: T-bills: Government exceeds target by 30%; interest rates decline again
items.description: The government exceeded its treasury bills target once again the week after the Minister of Finance presented the Mid-Year Budget Review last Thursday, 23 rd July 2026. According to the auction results released by the Bank of Ghana, the government achieved a 30.3% subscription in the T-bills auction. The government received bids worth GH¢12.3 billion. However, it accepted GH¢11.5 billion The 364-day bill was once again the most subscribed bill as GH¢8.1 billion of the bids were tendered, representing 65.5% of the total bids. The uptake was, however, GH¢7.8 billion. The 182-day bill received bids of GH¢1.3 billion. A little above GH¢1.1 billion was accepted. For the 91-day bill, GH¢2.9 billion of the bids were tendered. A little above GH¢2.6 billion of the bids were accepted. Meanwhile, interest rates fell on the yield curve. The yield on the 91-day bill went down by 11 basis points to 5.76%. That of the 182-day bill also decreased to 7.68% from the previous week’s 7.78%. Similarly, the yield on the 364-day dropped by 3.0 basis points to 12.96%. items.title: Man jailed 10 years for defiling seven-year-old boy in Wa
items.description: The Upper West Regional Police Command has secured the conviction and sentencing of a 42-year-old man for defiling a seven-year-old boy in Wa, following investigations by the Regional Domestic Violence and Victims Support Unit (DOVVSU). The convict, Elyasu Kunateh, was arrested on Tuesday, January 20, 2026, after the victim’s mother reported that the incident had occurred three days earlier, on Saturday, January 17, 2026. Following the report, police immediately launched investigations, referred the child to a medical facility for examination and ensured he received psychosocial support. The accused was subsequently arraigned before the Wa High Court and remanded into police custody pending trial. After a full hearing on Thursday, July 23, 2026, the court, presided over by His Lordship Justice Osei-Wusu Antwi, found Kunateh guilty of the offence. He was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment with hard labour. The Upper West Regional Police Command reaffirmed its commitment to protecting vulnerable persons and pledged to continue pursuing all reported cases of child abuse, sexual offences and gender-based violence. The Command also urged parents, guardians, caregivers and the general public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspected cases of abuse to the nearest police station for swift intervention.

items.title: Jeune ivoirien poignardé par une prostituée : Le récit tragique d’un rapport sexuel non payé qui vire au drame
items.description: Une nuit de débauche a viré au cauchemar sanglant ce samedi 26 juillet 2026. Dans le quartier Orange de Ouellé en Côte d'Ivoire, un différend portant sur une somme dérisoire de 3 000 FCFA a conduit au meurtre de Koffi Kouamé Marius, un jeune homme de 24 ans, poignardé lors d'une altercation avec une jeune femme. Ce drame a immédiatement mis le feu aux poudres, déclenchant des vagues de représailles contre les lieux de prostitution de la ville. Entre deuil brutal et colère populaire, l'intervention musclée de la gendarmerie a été nécessaire pour ramener un calme précaire, tandis qu'une enquête criminelle tente de démêler les fils de cette tragédie. Le calme habituel de la ville de Ouellé a été rompu par les sirènes de la gendarmerie et les cris de colère d'une jeunesse en deuil. Ce qui aurait dû rester une banale transaction nocturne s'est transformé en un crime qui secoue aujourd'hui toute la communauté. Tout commence aux alentours de 02 heures du matin, dans le quartier Orange. Selon les rapports de la gendarmerie, Koffi Kouamé Marius, 24 ans, ivoirien sans emploi, se rend au domicile de Purity Karibo, une Gabonaise de 22 ans, pour solliciter ses services. Le drame se noue à l'issue de leur rencontre. Koffi refuse de verser les 3 000 FCFA convenus, prétextant une insatisfaction quant à la prestation reçue. Le ton monte rapidement. Purity Karibo insiste pour obtenir son dû. Ce qui n'était qu'une discussion houleuse dégénère en une violente bagarre. Dans la confusion de la rixe, la jeune femme saisit un couteau et porte un coup critique au jeune homme, le blessant grièvement. Évacué d'urgence vers le Centre de Santé Urbain (CSU) de Ouellé, Koffi Kouamé Marius livre son dernier combat contre la mort pendant plusieurs heures. Il succombe finalement à ses blessures aux environs de 11 heures le même jour. L'annonce de son décès agit comme un détonateur dans la ville. Informés de la tragédie, des groupes de jeunes s'organisent spontanément pour mener des expéditions punitives. Leur cible : les établissements identifiés comme abritant des travailleuses du sexe. Ces représailles ont causé d'importants dégâts matériels, marquant la volonté de la jeunesse locale de se faire justice elle-même. Face au risque d'une escalade incontrôlable, les éléments de la gendarmerie sont intervenus rapidement sur les lieux des émeutes. Leur présence a permis de disperser les manifestants et de sécuriser les quartiers sensibles, évitant ainsi un bilan humain plus lourd. À l'heure actuelle, le calme est revenu, mais la tension reste palpable. Une enquête judiciaire a été officiellement ouverte par les autorités pour faire toute la lumière sur les circonstances exactes du meurtre et situer les responsabilités de chacun dans ce drame et les violences qui ont suivi. Ouellé pleure aujourd'hui un fils, victime d'une violence aussi absurde que foudroyante. items.title: Full List: Meet housemates of BBNaija season 11
items.description: BBNaija Season 11 officially got underway on Sunday as organisers unveiled the first set of housemates who will battle for the grand prize in this year’s edition of the reality TV show. From streamers and entrepreneurs to models and creatives, the contestants are arriving with distinct personalities, bold strategies and high expectations. Here is a look at latest BBNaija housemates: Tram Twenty-four-year-old streamer Tram from Lagos says he is entering Biggie’s house with one goal — winning. According to his profile, he has no interest in romance or distractions and intends to stay focused on the game. The organisers summed up his approach: “He’s tenacious to the core and here for one thing only — the game. No romance, no distractions, no apologies.” Temi Nkem At 21, Temi Nkem says she is bringing confidence and strategy into the BBNaija house. The organisers describe her as someone with a clear game plan who intends to play strictly by her own rules. “Temi Nkem is entering Biggie’s house with a game plan and plenty to say. She’s playing by Temi Nkem’s rules and that’s a strict programme.” Martins Martins, a 30-year-old visual storyteller and model from Kogi State, is swapping the runway for the BBNaija house. He describes his hidden talent as reading minds and says he is ready to enjoy the experience while wearing his heart on his sleeve. According to the organisers, “Martins from Kogi will be trading runway shows and catwalks for Biggie’s house… He is ready to have fun and he might wear his heart on his sleeve.” Mercedes Twenty-six-year-old Mercedes from Delta State is a massage therapist and concierge CEO. According to the organisers, she’s entering the BBNaija house with confidence and ambition, determined to add to her success rather than chase it. “She’s not chasing the bag, she’s adding another one.” Keivo Keivo, a 27-year-old web developer from Benue State, describes himself as a jack-of-all-trades with plenty of self-confidence. He says he is open to finding love in the house but is not thinking about marriage yet. His hobbies include gaming, painting and drawing. Chimsom Chuka Twenty-seven-year-old Chimsom Chuka, a pharmacist from Anambra State, says he is ready to enjoy every moment in Biggie’s house. The organisers describe him as patient and funny, adding that he wants to show viewers his authentic self while handling pressure with ease. Abi Abi, a chef and model from Osun State, says she is bringing humour and a vibrant personality to the competition. The organisers described her as “a certified scene-stealer”, adding: “Abi from Osun State isn’t here to do background roles. She’s bringing the big laughs and enough personality to season the entire BBNaija house. With the sauce.” Bells Twenty-two-year-old Bells is described as a resilient and independent contestant who is still in love with her high school sweetheart. A self-confessed rule follower, neat freak and foodie, she enters the BBNaija house hoping to stay true to herself despite whatever challenges lie ahead. Flora Flora is a makeup entrepreneur whose confidence matches her passion for fashion. According to the organisers, she is bringing honesty and plenty of spice into the competition. While her love life is described as “complicated,” she has little patience for insults and is expected to make her presence felt in the house. Aikou Twenty-five-year-old Aikou from Abuja is a freelance teacher and web developer who enjoys reading and is comfortable spending time on his own. Calm and outspoken, he says he is single and ready to fall in love again. However, the organisers note that dishonesty is one thing he cannot tolerate. Sultex Sultex, a 24-year-old dancer and choreographer from Lagos, says he is entering the BBNaija house with confidence and big dreams. He is known for speaking his mind and avoiding sugarcoating issues. His hobbies include gaming, dancing, table tennis and football, while he admits being a people pleaser is one of his weaknesses. He also says he dislikes liars. Kamsy Twenty-four-year-old Kamsy is an event planner and gift curator who says forgiveness does not come easily to her. She is bringing style, ambition, humour and just the right amount of drama into Biggie’s house as she competes for this season’s grand prize. Gerard Twenty-three-year-old Gerard is an on-air personality from Lagos who describes himself as a bundle of talent. An open book, Gerard says he hates dishonesty and plans to make the most of every moment in the BBNaija house. The organisers describe him as the house’s “wild card.” Oyin Oyin, 22, hails from Sagamu and is a sales entrepreneur and model. Proudly describing herself as “daddy’s girl,” she says she is ready to prove that first impressions can be misleading. With her sights firmly set on the grand prize, Oyin is entering the competition determined to make her mark. Sheba A gym enthusiast and proud mother, Sheba is bringing warmth, confidence and an open heart into Biggie’s house. The organisers describe her as someone who is ready for fun and is also open to finding love during her stay in the competition. Araga Fashion model Araga proudly calls himself a king and “the last loverboy standing in Nigeria.” He says he is entering the BBNaija house for the money, the energy and the possibility of finding love, while hoping his charisma will carry him far in the competition. items.title: Commémoration : la Maison de la Presse rend hommage à Babacar Touré
items.description: Six ans jour pour jour après la disparition de Babacar Touré, la Maison de la Presse qui porte désormais son nom a rendu un hommage solennel à celui qui demeure l’une des figures les plus marquantes du journalisme sénégalais. Le 26 juillet 2020, le Sénégal perdait le journaliste émérite, PDG et fondateur du Groupe Sud Communication. Une disparition qui avait profondément ému le monde des médias, tant l’homme avait contribué à façonner le paysage médiatique national à travers son engagement en faveur de la liberté de la presse, de la démocratie et du professionnalisme. Dans un communiqué publié ce samedi, la Maison de la Presse Babacar Touré a salué la mémoire d’un « visionnaire, bâtisseur et défenseur infatigable du droit à l’information ». L’institution souligne que son parcours exceptionnel continue d’inspirer plusieurs générations de journalistes au Sénégal et en Afrique. « Son œuvre, sa vision et ses valeurs continuent d’éclairer le chemin de la presse sénégalaise », indique le texte, rappelant l’attachement de Babacar Touré aux principes d’éthique, de responsabilité et d’indépendance dans l’exercice du métier. L’hommage revêt une portée particulière depuis que la Maison de la Presse porte officiellement le nom de Babacar Touré. Pour ses responsables, cette dénomination constitue un symbole fort de reconnaissance envers un homme qui a consacré sa vie à informer, former et défendre la liberté d’expression. En cette date anniversaire, l’institution a également renouvelé son engagement à préserver et promouvoir les idéaux incarnés par son illustre parrain. Des prières ont été formulées pour le repos de son âme, dans une atmosphère de recueillement et de gratitude. Au-delà de l’émotion, cette commémoration rappelle l’empreinte durable laissée par Babacar Touré sur le journalisme sénégalais. Fondateur d’un groupe de presse devenu une référence, il aura marqué son époque par son courage, sa rigueur et sa conviction que l’information est un pilier essentiel de la démocratie. Six ans après sa disparition, son héritage continue de vivre à travers les médias qu’il a contribué à bâtir, mais aussi à travers les nombreux professionnels qu’il a inspirés et formés au fil des décennies.

items.title: Magal 2026 : le président Bassriou Diomaye Faye annonce l’accélération d’un programme de 60 milliards FCfa pour Touba
items.description: Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a effectué, dimanche 26 juillet 2026, sa traditionnelle visite de pré-Magal auprès du khalife général des mourides, Serigne Mountakha Mbacké. Accompagné du Premier ministre, du ministre de l'Intérieur, de plusieurs membres du gouvernement et de collaborateurs de son cabinet, il a été accueilli par les autorités administratives et religieuses de Touba, notamment le porte-parole du khalife, Serigne Bassirou Mbacké Abdou Khadre. Le chef de l'État a exprimé sa profonde reconnaissance envers le khalife général, qu'il considère comme un guide, un père et un conseiller. Évoquant le sens de sa visite, il a rappelé que l'exil de Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba était un acte de dévouement exclusif envers Dieu et le Prophète Mouhamed (PSL), un héritage spirituel qui, selon lui, est aujourd'hui préservé par Serigne Mountakha Mbacké. Il a salué le rôle de « régulateur social » joué par le khalife et formulé des prières pour sa santé et sa longévité. Le président est également revenu sur les projets engagés par l'État pour accompagner le développement de Touba, confrontée à une forte croissance démographique. Il a cité la réalisation de quatre nouveaux forages pour renforcer l'approvisionnement en eau potable et annoncé le déploiement d'une cinquantaine de camions-citernes durant le Grand Magal. En matière d'assainissement, il a rappelé qu'un programme de 60 milliards de francs CFA est en cours, avec une première phase consacrée au drainage gravitaire des eaux pluviales. Les travaux concernent notamment les bassins de rétention de Darou Rahmane et de Pofdy ainsi que les alentours de la Grande Mosquée. Avant de quitter Touba, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a sollicité les prières du khalife pour la paix, la cohésion sociale et la prospérité du Sénégal. Prenant la parole au nom du khalife, Serigne Bassirou Mbacké Abdou Khadre s'est réjoui de cette visite et a salué les efforts consentis par l'État en faveur de Touba. Il a encouragé le président à poursuivre les investissements dans des secteurs prioritaires comme l'hydraulique, l'assainissement et l'enseignement supérieur, tout en appelant à étendre cette dynamique aux autres foyers religieux du pays. Il a enfin rappelé la portée spirituelle du Grand Magal et insisté sur la responsabilité du chef de l'État dans la préservation de la paix et de la cohésion nationale. Birane Diop, correspondant

items.title: L’agression d’une femme musulmane devant son fils de 7 ans bouleverse le Canada
items.description: Une vidéo d'une rare violence circule sur les réseaux sociaux. On y voit une femme frapper une femme musulmane , devant son fils, à plusieurs reprises sur un parking dans une ville du Canada. Selon les premiers éléments, l'agression serait d’origine islamophobe. La scène se déroule sur un parking à Moncton, dans la province canadienne du Nouveau-Brunswick. Une femme s'approche de la victime avant de lui asséner plusieurs coups de poing à la tête. La victime tente de fuir, mais n’y arrive pas. Malgré la présence de plusieurs personnes autour, aucune n'est intervenue. Le fils de la victime, présent au moment des faits, assiste à l'agression de sa mère. L’agression d’une musulmane devant son fils de 7 ans suscite une vive émotion au Canada Selon son mari, relayé par la Moncton Muslim Association, la femme agressée aurait été visée en raison de sa religion. FLASH INFO — « Retournez dans votre pays » : une mère musulmane tabassée devant son fils de 7 ans à Moncton À Moncton, une musulmane a été brutalement agressée devant son fils de 7 ans par des individus qui hurlaient des insultes racistes. Cet acte odieux à caractère… pic.twitter.com/JnbnAWw59S — Focus (@FocusMedia_Fr) July 22, 2026 Dans un communiqué, la Moncton Muslim Association est revenue sur les circonstances de l'agression en s'appuyant sur le témoignage du mari de la victime. Selon ce document, la mère de famille a été agressée sous les yeux de son fils de 7 ans. Le président de l'association, Ali Ettrarnichi, s'est exprimé au micro d'Ici Radio-Canada. « La femme et son fils sont vraiment choqués, mentalement et émotionnellement. Ils sont traumatisés, surtout l'enfant », a-t-il expliqué. D'après le média canadien, les faits se sont produits en début de soirée. Une enquête a été ouverte par la Gendarmerie royale du Canada afin de déterminer « si la haine a joué un rôle dans l'incident ». La vidéo a rapidement fait le tour des réseaux sociaux et suscité de nombreuses réactions. La Première ministre du Nouveau-Brunswick, Susan Holt, a réagi dans une publication sur son compte Facebook. « Je suis profondément bouleversée par l'attaque violente et haineuse commise contre une femme musulmane à Moncton », a-t-elle écrit. Elle a ajouté être aux côtés de la victime, de sa famille et de l'ensemble de la communauté musulmane, tout en souhaitant un prompt rétablissement à la femme agressée. Susan Holt a également affirmé que personne ne devrait être pris pour cible en raison de sa foi, de sa race ou de son pays d'origine. « Il n'y a pas de place pour l'islamophobie ou pour toute autre forme de haine au Nouveau-Brunswick. De tels actes ne reflètent pas qui nous sommes », a-t-elle conclu. L'enquête est toujours en cours. La police demande à toute personne ayant été témoin de l'agression ou disposant d'informations ou d'images de se manifester auprès de ses services. L’article L'agression d'une femme musulmane devant son fils de 7 ans bouleverse le Canada est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: ORAL is still working and prosecuting corruption cases – Deputy AG
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, has dismissed claims that the Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) initiative is no longer active, insisting that the team is still working to pursue cases arising from its investigations. According to him, ORAL has continued to support efforts to prosecute alleged cases of corruption and recover public resources since its establishment. Speaking on The Law on JoyNews with Samson Lardy Anyenini on Sunday, July 26, Dr Srem-Sai said the initiative has been effective in ensuring that cases identified through its work are pursued through the appropriate legal processes. “ORAL is still working,” he said. He explained that the initiative has contributed to the identification and prosecution of several cases, adding that one of the outcomes of its work is the prosecution of the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, commonly known as Chairman Wontumi. “We started Wontumi in January; by the middle of March, we had closed our case. We have finished with Wontumi. Where has it happened before that a case has gone through trial between the middle of January and been done within two months? So ORAL is working,” he noted. Background On July 20, the Accra High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years’ imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region. READ ALSO: Court convicts Wontumi on six illegal mining charges over Samreboi concession Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay, who presided over the Criminal Division of the High Court, delivered the sentence shortly after 11:40 am on Monday, July 20, 2026, bringing to an end one of the country’s most closely watched illegal mining prosecutions. The court also imposed a fine of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000, with a default sentence of three years’ imprisonment if the fine is not paid.

items.title: Deputy AG alleges ‘deliberate campaign’ to misrepresent Adu-Boahene prosecution
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, has alleged that there is a deliberate public and media campaign to misrepresent the criminal case against former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General, Kwabena Adu-Boahene, insisting that the prosecution’s case is straightforward. According to him, the charges are based on allegations that public funds earmarked for the purchase of defence equipment were diverted into a private account and subsequently used for personal acquisitions. Speaking on The Law with Samson Lardy Anyenini on JoyNews on Sunday, July 26, Dr Srem-Sai dismissed suggestions that the case was complex, saying the facts before the court were clear. “I think there’s a very determined public campaign, media campaign, to create an impression. It’s a simple case, Samson.” In 2025, the Attorney-General Dominic Ayine formally charged Mr Adu-Boahene and his wife, Angela Adjei Boateng, over corruption offences involving an amount of GHS49 million. Together with two others, Mildred Donkor and Advantage Solutions Limited, they are accused of 11 counts of offences, including stealing, money laundering, defrauding by false pretences, and wilfully causing financial loss. According to the writ filed at the High Court on Wednesday, April 30, 2025, Mr Adu-Boahene, who was responsible for overseeing critical national security infrastructure, including contracts with foreign companies, signed a deal with an Israeli company, ISC Holdings Limited, to purchase cyber defence software for $7 million. In total, Adu-Boahene is alleged to have transferred approximately GHS 49 million (around $7 million) from the NSB’s funds into his personal accounts, falsely justifying these transactions as payments for the cyber defence systems, together with his accomplice. Dr Srem-Sai explained on the show that the prosecution’s case centres on the alleged movement of the public funds from a government account into a private account under the pretext of procuring defence equipment for the state. “There is public money in a public account. You have moved the public money from the public account into a private account and told the bank which did the transaction that you are using the money to go and purchase defence equipment for the state.” Dr Srem-Sai said evidence gathered by the prosecution showed that the funds were instead allegedly spent on private assets. “The evidence shows from the account into which you deposited the money that you spent the money to buy houses for yourself and other high-end cars which you were renting and using for your own good.” He maintained that the alleged conduct amounted to criminal offences involving public funds. “Our case is simple. You cannot do this with public money. It amounts to stealing or causing financial loss or any of the public financial offences. That is what we are charging for.” The Deputy Attorney-General also accused the defence of attempting to shape public opinion outside the courtroom while the trial was ongoing. He said, unlike the defence, he had deliberately refrained from commenting publicly on the merits of the case after court proceedings. “I have decided that I will not step out of court and grant interviews. But it doesn’t mean that when my opponent steps out of court and grants interviews, whatever he is saying to the public is sacrosanct.” Dr Srem-Sai further disclosed that one of the defence’s initial arguments was that the funds transferred into Adu-Boahene’s private account constituted repayment of loans he had allegedly advanced to a public institution. “They first started by saying that it was a loan. I’m sure you heard about that, that he gives loans to the public institution, and so the money moving back into his account is a repayment of the loan.” His remarks come as the trial of Mr Adu-Boahene continues, with the prosecution seeking to prove that public funds intended for national security procurement were unlawfully diverted for private use.

BURKINA/Académie militaire Georges Namoano : la 25e promotion baptisée « Lieutenant Sawadogo Alexandre Bienvenu » reçoit ses épaulettes de sous-lieutenant
items.description: BURKINA-NAHOURI-DÉFENSE-ACADÉMIE-CÉRÉMONIE-SORTIE-PROMOTION BURKINA/Académie militaire Georges Namoano : la 25e promotion baptisée « Lieutenant Sawadogo Alexandre Bienvenu » reçoit ses épaulettes de sous-lieutenant Ouagadougou, 25 juil. 2026 (AIB) – Le Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a présidé, samedi à Pô, la cérémonie de remise d'épaulettes aux Élèves-Officiers d'Active (EOA) de la 25e promotion de l'Académie militaire Georges Namoano (AMGN), baptisée « Lieutenant Sawadogo Alexandre Bienvenu » en hommage à cet officier tombé au champ d'honneur en février 2022. Deux cent dix-sept (217) nouveaux sous-lieutenants, dont 199 Burkinabè et 18 ressortissants de neuf pays amis (Cameroun, Centrafrique, Djibouti, Guinée, Mali, Niger, Sénégal, Tchad et Togo), ont été proclamés aptes à servir au terme de 21 mois de formation, avec une moyenne générale de promotion de 14,28/20. La promotion est parrainée par le Général de brigade Kassoum Coulibaly, ancien ministre chargé de la Défense et actuel ambassadeur du Burkina Faso aux États-Unis d'Amérique. Pour la première fois, la cérémonie s'est tenue sur le site de la Nouvelle Académie, dont les nouvelles infrastructures composées de salles de cours, de dortoirs, d'amphithéâtre de 500 places, de réfectoire moderne et autres équipements pédagogiques qui accueilleront les prochaines promotions dès la rentrée académique. Les nouveaux officiers ont revêtu, pour l'occasion, une tenue en pagne traditionnel gourmantché, portée à l'issue des rites d'initiation dans l'Est du Burkina Faso. Le Chef d'État-major général des armées, le Général de division Moussa Diallo, a salué les excellents résultats enregistrés par la promotion et assuré le Président du Faso que les élèves-officiers étaient dignes d'être élevés au grade de sous-lieutenant. Il les a exhortés à être des chefs exemplaires, refusant « la facilité, l'arrogance, la corruption et la trahison », tout en rappelant que le commandement consiste avant tout à montrer l'exemple et à inspirer ses hommes dans les moments les plus difficiles. Le Commandant de l'Académie militaire Georges Namoano, le Lieutenant-colonel William Desmond Baguéra, a, pour sa part, souligné que la tenue de cette cérémonie sur le nouveau site concrétise une promesse faite un an plus tôt et traduit la volonté des autorités de doter le Burkina Faso d'un outil de formation militaire à la hauteur des défis sécuritaires actuels. Il a invité les futurs officiers à servir avec dignité, à commander avec justice et à combattre avec honneur, affirmant que « le véritable chef n'est pas celui qui commande, mais celui qui inspire ». Au nom de ses camarades, le délégué de la promotion,Abdallah Cédric Ki, est revenu sur les 21 mois d'une formation marquée par des stages spécialisés en tir de combat, lutte contre les engins explosifs improvisés (IED), techniques command9o, combat motorisé et renseignement opérationnel. Se disant pleinement préparé aux exigences du terrain, il a assuré que les nouveaux sous-lieutenants combattront « jusqu'au dernier retranchement de l'ennemi » pour défendre la souveraineté nationale. Il a également rendu hommage à un camarade décédé au cours de la formation ainsi qu'à la population du Nahouri pour son hospitalité. Agence d'information du Burkina NAK/yos
